description: Every user-facing surface of the frontend, with the backend capability and contract behind it. This is the registry's vocabulary: a capability may only attach to a surface declared here. Status is honest: 'present' (implemented), 'partial' (implemented with declared 501 gaps), 'unsupported' (renders, backend not implemented).

surfaces.title: Sign-in, owner setup and session screens
surfaces.notes: Owned by the auth LEGO (P2). The frontend contract only consumes its envelopes and session rules.

surfaces.title: Application shell — header, main sidebar, settings sidebar, breadcrumbs
surfaces.notes: Entry visibility is scope- and flag-driven (P2 §10.3); the frontend must never hide a surface to fake capability.

surfaces.title: Home — workflow list/overview
surfaces.notes: Insights/data-table widgets on this surface are unimplemented backend capabilities and answer 501 (compatibility layer), never a fake empty payload.

surfaces.title: Settings pages (personal, users, API, security, usage, …)
surfaces.notes: P2 made the pages reachable and honest: reachable pages whose backend is not implemented answer 501 {code:'unsupported'} with owner/phase metadata.

surfaces.title: Workflow canvas (nodes, connections, panel)
surfaces.notes: The canvas is the reference surface for interaction contracts: save/run/execute-step must keep the P0-verified behavior.

surfaces.title: Node creator / node menu (palette, search, descriptions)
surfaces.notes: Community nodes / dynamic parameters behind this surface are unimplemented capabilities (501 with owner 'node-registry'/'dynamic-parameters'); the stock palette itself is complete (483 node types).

surfaces.title: Credentials list, credential editor and credential modal
surfaces.notes: OAuth1/OAuth2 flows and credential resolvers are unimplemented capabilities (501).

surfaces.title: Execution list, execution detail and execution errors
surfaces.notes: Error text from the engine arrives through the error model: code first, message as fallback (translation-ready).

surfaces.title: Webhook and form endpoints (triggers, test URLs, activation state)
surfaces.notes: Endpoint URLs are published in settings; trigger routing itself is tracked by the webhook/scheduler roadmap items and is not part of the frontend boundary.

surfaces.title: Toasts, banners, push-driven updates and system messages
surfaces.notes: Push event names and payload keys are contract data (contract.mjs EVENTS); the frontend never invents its own channel.

surfaces.title: Modals and overlays (workflow settings, credential modal, confirmations)
surfaces.notes: Frontend-owned surface: dialogs carry no backend capability of their own, they render data whose capability belongs to another surface.

surfaces.title: Error presentation — page-level errors, toasts, node/execution errors, unsupported capability notices
surfaces.notes: The single place where a backend error code becomes a displayable message; today the fallback text, later the localized one.

surfaces.title: Workflow canvas — nodes, edges, viewport and selection
surfaces.notes: P2-S14 Layer 3 strangler slice (issue #240): composite region of the workflow editor delivered as its own pilot. The graph model is handed over to the frontend-lego canvas surface; the frontend never fetches a graph, performs no engine call and never mutates the workflow document.

surfaces.title: Node parameter / NDV panel (one node type's parameters)
surfaces.notes: P2-S15 Layer 3 strangler slice (issue #240): the parameter panel that edits one node type's parameters through the parameter contract. Definitions and values are handed over; expression evaluation stays behind the declared boundary - the frontend never evaluates and never posts the workflow.

surfaces.title: Connection inspector — a workflow's connections over handed-over records
surfaces.notes: P2-S16 Layer 3 strangler slice (issue #240): the connection inspector / connection list delivered as its own pilot. Connection records and the node-id vocabulary are handed over; the frontend never fetches a graph, performs no engine call and never writes the workflow - selection is view state, reconnect and remove are declared requests with closed results.

surfaces.title: Environments - selection + variable scoping (handed-over records)
surfaces.notes: P2-S18 Layer 4 strangler slice (issue #240): the environment selection and variable-scoping panel delivered as its own pilot. Environments, the active id and the variable records are handed over; the frontend never fetches variables, never derives the active environment locally (request-switch is declared - only a fresh hand-over moves it) and never persists (set/set-scope/submit are declared with closed results).

surfaces.title: Integrations - external sources view (handed-over records, install behind admission)
surfaces.notes: P2-S19 Layer 4 strangler slice (issue #240): the external integration management panel (community/private/custom sources view) delivered as its own pilot. Integrations and the active id are handed over; the frontend never fetches and never installs - request-install is declared and always lands behind the P6 admission path (closed results, never a local install).

surfaces.title: Execution management - retry/stop/bulk over handed-over records
surfaces.notes: P2-S20 Layer 4 strangler slice (issue #240): the retry/stop/bulk actions around executions, beyond the P2-S06 history list, delivered as its own pilot. Execution records are handed over; the frontend never fetches and never mutates a record - request-retry/request-stop/request-bulk-* are declared with closed results and the execution capability (app layer) performs every action. The selection is view state cleared by every fresh hand-over.

surfaces.title: Project/workspace administration - membership and project data handed over
surfaces.notes: P2-S21 Layer 4 strangler slice (issue #240): the project and workspace administration panels. Membership and project data are handed over; the surface holds no project model of its own until P5-M11 exists - no fetch, no record mutation, no direct call to the project/role capability. invite/remove/rename are declared with closed results; the selected project is view state cleared by every fresh hand-over.

surfaces.title: AI Assistant - conversational turns handed over as events
surfaces.notes: P2-S22 Layer 5 strangler slice (issue #240): the conversational assistant surface. Assistant turns are handed over as events - the surface never fabricates assistant output: no method writes a turn and no inference/provider client exists here. request-send and request-stop-stream are declared with closed results; the capability that owns inference performs them and the reply arrives only via a fresh hand-over.

surfaces.title: AI Copilot - inline suggestions accepted or rejected explicitly
surfaces.notes: P2-S23 Layer 5 strangler slice (issue #240): the inline copilot suggestion surface. Suggestions arrive as declared AI capability events through hand-over - the surface never applies a suggestion silently: no method writes a status, accept/reject are declared with closed results, and the outcome arrives only via a fresh hand-over. No fetch, no inference client, no persistence.

surfaces.title: AI Node - model catalog handed over from the node/parameter contracts
surfaces.notes: P2-S24 Layer 5 strangler slice (issue #240): the AI-node parameter and model-picker surfaces. The model catalog is handed over from the node/parameter contracts; the surface holds no second source of truth - no fetch, no catalog mutation, no local write of the selected model. request-select-model is declared with closed results and the new value arrives only via a fresh hand-over.

surfaces.title: Work Trace - handed-over execution timeline (read-only)
surfaces.notes: P2-S25 Layer 5 strangler slice (issue #240): the work-trace timeline surface. Trace events are handed over from the observability capability; the surface holds no second source of truth - no fetch, no event mutation, no navigation. request-open-event is declared with closed results and the owning capability performs the navigation.

surfaces.title: Memory/Context/Session views - handed-over inspection state (read-only)
surfaces.notes: P2-S26 Layer 5 strangler slice (issue #240): the memory/context/session inspection surfaces. Session state is handed over from the session capability; the surface holds no private data path - no direct session store access, no fetch, no record mutation, no navigation. request-open-entry is declared with closed results and the owning capability performs the navigation.

surfaces.title: Skills/Capabilities - handed-over catalog (read-only, grants nothing)
surfaces.notes: P2-S27 Layer 5 strangler slice (issue #240): the skills and capability catalog surfaces. The catalog is handed over from the capability registry; the surface holds no private data path and GRANTS NOTHING - no direct registry access, no fetch, no record mutation, no navigation. request-open-skill is declared with closed results and the owning capability performs the navigation.
